summary: Iteration 4 (keyword-based fast matching) regression: 26/26 backend pytest tests PASS in ~33s against the live preview URL. Re-ran the full iteration-2 suite (17 tests, all green) and added 9 new tests covering (a) enriched resume parse fields (skills, adjacent_skills, role_titles, years_experience, summary), (b) GET /api/jobs?min_score=20 returns only score>=20 jobs sorted DESC and in <5s, (c) GET /api/jobs?min_score=0 returns everything with best_match populated and per-resume matches[], (d) min_score actually trims the result set, (e) AI deep-score via POST /api/jobs/{id}/match flips best_match.source from 'keyword' to 'ai' on the next /jobs read, (f) user with 0 resumes gets ALL jobs unfiltered (has_resumes=False short-circuits), and (g) pure-Python unit tests for services/matching.keyword_score + best_match (positive match, zero match, multi-resume winner pick). Measured GET /api/jobs?min_score=20 latency ~1.0-1.5s for the live pool (111+ jobs) — matches the dev's ~1.2s smoke test claim.

minor.issue: Two-pass sort in server.py (lines 326-328) — first sort is unused/no-op because the second sort overrides it. Harmless but dead code; the second `out.sort(key=lambda j: ((score, posted_at)), reverse=True)` does the job. Remove the first sort to avoid confusion.

Error string still references the removed 'AI Match all' button on the dashboard (Iteration 4 explicitly removed it per Dashboard.jsx changes). Update message to: 'Open a few jobs and run Deep AI re-score first.'

Single-letter / 1-2 char skills could match noise via _phrase_present substring fallback (e.g. 'C' as a skill matches every word containing c). Consider min-length guard or token-only matching for short keywords.
(Carried over) allow_origins='*' + allow_credentials=True is spec-invalid; works only because preview is same-origin.

action_items: (Optional polish) Remove the redundant first sort in /app/backend/server.py list_jobs (lines 326-327).
(Optional polish) Update /api/digest/send error string — 'AI Match all' button no longer exists.
(Optional hardening) Add min-length guard for short keyword phrases in services/matching._phrase_present to avoid substring false positives on 1-2 char skills.
critical_code_review_comments: services/matching.py is clean, pure-Python, deterministic and fast — verified ~1.2s for 111-job pool. Scoring formula (base + title_bonus + role_bonus, capped at 100) behaves sanely on unit fixtures.
services/llm.py parse_resume_ai now logs exceptions (good — fix from iter-2 minor) and returns all 5 enriched fields with proper coercion + slicing caps.

server.py list_jobs correctly short-circuits filtering when has_resumes=False (verified via test_no_resumes_returns_all_jobs_unfiltered). AI matches override keyword score on a per-job basis (verified end-to-end).
Resume model now exposes adjacent_skills/role_titles/years_experience/summary — backward-compat-safe (defaults provided).
All endpoints from iteration 2 still green; no regressions introduced by the matching rework.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_applymate_au.py (added 9 tests for keyword-matching engine; added sys.path shim for service unit imports)
test_credentials: Per /app/memory/test_credentials.md — Mongo-injected session created in seed_user fixture; cleaned up after suite.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `cd /app && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://jobhunt-agent.preview.emergentagent.com python -m pytest backend/tests/test_applymate_au.py -v` — expect 26/26 in ~33s. Note: tests are intentionally ordered (sequential dependency on RESUME_ID created in test_upload_resume), so DO NOT use pytest-xdist or -k single-test runs for the iteration-4 keyword tests — they assume a resume has been uploaded in this session. The new test_no_resumes_returns_all_jobs_unfiltered spins up its own isolated user. Frontend skipped per review_request testing_type='backend only'.
rca of the issue: No regression detected. The single mid-run failure during development was a test-ordering artifact (test_match in iter-2 had already AI-scored the first tech job, so test_ai_deep_score_then_source_becomes_ai needed to pick a job that was still keyword-only). Fixed by filtering candidates where best_match.source=='keyword' and ai_matches is empty.
